{{Term/Store|Stone Talus|Stone Taluses|Series, BotW, TotK, CoH, AoC, AoI}},{{Exp Game|BotW, TotK, CoH, AoC, AoI}}<ref name="BotW Hyrule Compendium"/><ref name="TotK Hyrule Compendium"/><ref name="CoH Game Over"/><ref name="AoC Game Screen"/><ref name="AoI Game Screen"/> also known as '''Stone Colossuses''',{{Exp Game|BotW}}<ref name="BotW Kilton 2"/> are recurring [[Boss]]es and [[Sub-Boss]]es in {{TLoZ Series}}.

==Characteristics==
==={{BotW|-}}===
{{Compendium/Extract|Stone Talus}}
Stone Taluses appear as a cluster of boulders at first, but once approached, they assemble into large golem-like beings.<ref name="BotW Hyrule Compendium 2"/> [[Stone Talus (Luminous)|Luminous]], [[Stone Talus (Rare)|Rare]], [[Frost Talus|Frost]], and [[Igneo Talus|Igneo]] variations can also be found all around [[Hyrule]]. In addition to these, two unique Stone Taluses known as the [[Stone Talus (Junior)]] and [[Stone Talus (Senior)]] can be found on opposite sides of the [[Dueling Peaks]].

Stone Taluses are fairly large compared and deal important amounts of damage.{{How Many}} They are very slow-moving, so as long as [[Link]] stays behind or beneath them, he will be out of harm's way. Stone Taluses can use their large arm structures to punch and swipe across the ground, dealing heavy damage to the impact area. They can also fall forward and crash their entire body into the ground or launch large fragments of their rocky frame at Link. 

To defeat a Stone Talus, Link can climb onto its body and attack the [[Ore Deposit]] on its back, usually located on top or at the back of the [[Sub-Boss]].<ref name="BotW Hyrule Compendium 2"/> Link can inflict double damage using a two-handed [[Weapon]], or four times as much damage using an [[Iron Sledgehammer]]. After taking damage, Stone Taluses attempt to throw Link off by shaking themselves. To make climbing easier, Link can use a [[Remote Bomb]] to blast apart its arms, hindering it temporarily. Stone Taluses regenerate lost body parts shortly after losing them. Alternatively, Link can stun the Stone Talus by shooting the [[Ore Deposit]] on its back, making it fall on its face. Upon being defeated, a Stone Talus leaves behind a variety of [[Gem]]s, depending of its type.

After Link has beaten [[Calamity Ganon]] from the first time, he will be able to talk to [[Kilton]] about Stone Taluses.<ref name="BotW Kilton 2"/> Though Kilton is currently studying them, he has been unable to approach due to their gigantic size, so he asks Link to defeat all of the Stone Taluses in Hyrule on his behalf so that he can analyze the scent their fluids leave behind.<ref name="BotW Kilton 3"/> If Link achieves this goal, Kilton will reward him with the [[Medal of Honor: Talus]].<ref name="BotW Kilton 4"/> This research helps Kilton learn about the musculoskeletal structure and diet of Stone Taluses.<ref name="BotW Kilton 5"/>

==={{TotK|-}}===
{{Compendium/Extract/TotK|Stone Talus}}
Stone Taluses appear as Enemies in {{TotK}}. Their health has been slightly increased. A new variant called the [[Battle Talus]] is also introduced, which are Stone Taluses that are modified to function as a mobile [[Monster Stronghold]] replete with chevaux de frise on the undersides of their wooden frames to prevent intruders from climbing.

==Other Appearances==
==={{CoH|-}}===
{{Noncanon|Start}}
Stone Taluses are two tiles wide and move every third beat. They have 3 [[Heart Container]]s, but must be hit multiple times to crack them, allowing their [[Heart]]s to be reduced, unless the character's [[Weapon]] has piercing. If the character is next to the Stone Talus the beat before it moves, it will use an area attack, hitting all eight adjacent tiles. If the Stone Talus is not hit for a while, it will sit still and become immune to attacks while it reforms itself, regaining lost Hearts.
